Masha'Allah, this home is so bright! (compliment said when entering)
Permission to enter? (polite way to ask before stepping in)
Your home is blessed (complimenting the home)
After you (gesturing for elders to enter first)
Welcome, welcome (warm response to guest)
Come in, come in (urging guest to enter)
God keep you safe (response to 'welcome')
Make yourself at home (casual, to peers)
You honor us (humble response to welcome)
I’m so happy to be here (warm, sincere)
You’re my heart (intimate, to partner only)
My name is... (formal, to elders)
What's your name? (polite, to elders)
This is my mother (introducing her respectfully)
This is my father (introducing him respectfully)
How should I address your mother? (asking partner)
Call her 'Mama' (partner telling you what to say)
This is my aunt (father's sister, respectful)
This is my uncle (father's brother, respectful)
This is my aunt (mother's sister, respectful)
This is my uncle (mother's brother, respectful)
What do I call your older brother? (asking partner)
vocab.franco: A5ook el kbeer anadih bi eih?

vocab.en: No, thank you (first polite refusal).
I swear I'm full (after second helping).
Just a little, please (when they insist).
It's delicious, may God bless your hands (praise to the cook).
I can't eat another bite (polite way to stop).
You're spoiling me (when they keep insisting).
I'll have some later (gentle refusal).
It's perfect, no need for more (warm but firm).
I'll explode if I eat more (humorous refusal).
Just a sip, I'm really full (for tea/juice).
You're too kind (to the host after insistence).
I'm from [country/city], originally.
I work in [field], but I'm still learning.
vocab.ar: بشتغل في [مجال]، بس لسه بتعلّم عربي.

vocab.en: My family's small—just my parents and me.
vocab.ar: عيلتي صغيرة، بابا وماما وأنا بس.
vocab.franco: 3eelti soghayyara, baba w mama w ana bass.

vocab.en: I’ve been in Egypt for [time], and I love it here.
vocab.ar: أنا في مصر بقالي [مدة]، وبحبها أوي.
vocab.franco: Ana fi Masr ba2aly [modda], w ba7ebha awy.

vocab.en: I’m staying until [time], God willing.
My Arabic is still weak, but I’m trying!
I have one brother/sister—just us two.
vocab.ar: لي أخ/أخت واحد بس، إحنا الاتنين.
vocab.franco: Li akh/okht wa7ed bass, e7na el-etnein.

vocab.en: I’m here to learn and be part of the family.
vocab.ar: أنا جاي أتعلم وأبقى واحد من العيلة.
vocab.franco: Ana gay at3allam w ab2a wa7ed men el-3eela.

vocab.en: I love Egyptian food—it’s the best!
vocab.ar: بحب الأكل المصري أوي، أحسن حاجة!

vocab.en: I’m so happy to meet you all!
I’m still getting used to Cairo—it’s amazing!
vocab.ar: لسه بتعود على القاهرة… بس حلوة قوي!

vocab.en: This home is so full of blessings, God willing.
vocab.ar: ما شاء الله البيت ده مليان بركة.
vocab.franco: Ma sha2 Allah el-beet da melyan baraka.

vocab.en: Your hands are blessed, may God keep them safe.
The food is incredible, may God bless your hands.
vocab.ar: الأكل ده تحفة، ربنا يبارك في إيدك.
vocab.franco: El-akl da to7fa, rabena ybarek fe eedak.

vocab.en: What a beautiful home, God protect it.
vocab.ar: البيت ده جميل أوي، الله يحميه.
vocab.franco: El-beet da gameel awy, Allah ye7mayo.

vocab.en: The kids are so well-mannered, God bless them.
vocab.ar: العيال مهذبين أوي، ربنا يبارك فيهم.
vocab.franco: El-3eyal mohazbeen awy, rabena ybarek feehom.

vocab.en: You’ve raised them so well, may God reward you.
This dish is amazing, your hands are golden!
vocab.ar: الأكل ده حاجة حلوة أوي، إيدك دهب!

vocab.en: The house smells so good, like heaven!
vocab.ar: البيت ريحته حلوة أوي، زي الجنة!

vocab.en: You’re all so kind, God bless this family.
vocab.ar: أنتم طيبين أوي، ربنا يبارك في العيلة دي.
vocab.franco: Entom taybeen awy, rabena ybarek fel-3eela di.

vocab.en: The kids are adorable, ma sha’ Allah!
vocab.ar: العيال حلوين أوي، ما شاء الله!

vocab.en: I feel so welcome here, thank God.
vocab.ar: أنا حاسس نفسي في بيتي، الحمد لله.
vocab.franco: Ana 7ases nafsi fe beety, el-7amd lellah.

vocab.en: Do you like Egypt?
Can you handle the spice?
When are you learning Arabic?
vocab.ar: حضرتك بتتعلم عربي بقالك قد إيه؟

vocab.en: When’s the wedding?
Do you eat ful medames?
Are you used to the heat yet?
You’re not leaving us, right?
Do you like Egyptian tea?
You’ll visit us often, won’t you?
You’re not scared of our family, are you?
vocab.ar: مش خايف من العيلة بتاعتنا، صح؟

vocab.en: You’ll get used to us soon, inshallah.
vocab.ar: هتتعود علينا قريب إن شاء الله.

vocab.en: I didn’t catch that—could you say it again, please?
vocab.ar: معلش، ممكن تقولها تاني لو سمحت؟
vocab.franco: Ma3lesh, momken t2olha tani law sama7t?

vocab.en: Sorry, my Arabic is still weak—could you speak a little slower?
vocab.ar: آسف، عربيتي لسه ضعيفة… ممكن تتكلم أبطأ شوية؟
vocab.franco: Asif, 3arabiti lissa da3eefa... momken tetkallem abTa2 shwayya?

vocab.en: I missed that—what did you say?
vocab.ar: ما سمعتش كويس… إيه اللي حضرتك قلته؟
vocab.franco: Ma seme3tesh kwayyes... eh elli hadratak 2olto?

vocab.en: Could you repeat that one more time?
I didn’t get it—could you explain in simpler words?
vocab.ar: ما فهمتش، ممكن تشرحي بكلمات أسهل؟
vocab.franco: Ma fhmtish, momken teshra7i b kalemat as-hal?

vocab.en: Wait, I’m lost—what’s going on?
vocab.ar: استنى، انا تايه، ايه اللي بيحصل؟
vocab.franco: Estanna, ana tayeh, eih elly bey7sal?

vocab.en: Babe, translate this for me quick.
I didn’t understand—could you say it in English?
vocab.franco: Ma fhmtish, momken t2olha bel engelizi?

vocab.en: Hold on, I need to ask [partner’s name] what this means.
vocab.ar: استنى، لازم اسأل [اسم الشريك] ده معناه ايه.
vocab.franco: Estanna, lazem as2al [esm el shareek] da ma3nah eih.

vocab.en: Sorry, my brain froze—could you repeat?
I’m trying to follow, but it’s too fast.
vocab.ar: بحاول أتابع بس الكلام سريع أوي.
vocab.franco: Ba7awel atabe3 bas el-kalam saree3 awy.

vocab.en: Oops, my tongue got tangled!
Sorry, my brain short-circuited for a second!
I swear I’m not usually this clumsy… today’s just not my day!
vocab.ar: والله ما أنا كده عادة… النهارده مش يومي!
vocab.franco: WAllah ma ana keda 3ada… elnaharda msh yomi!

vocab.en: Forgive me, I’m still learning the Egyptian way!
vocab.ar: سامحني، أنا لسه بتعلّم اللهجة المصرية.
vocab.franco: Same7ni, ana lissa bet3allam el-lahga el-masreyya.

vocab.en: Oh no, did I just say that out loud? My bad!
vocab.ar: يا نهار أبيض… أنا قلت كده بصوت عالي؟ معلش!
vocab.franco: Ya nahar abyad... ana 2olt keda be-sot 3ali? ma3lesh!

vocab.en: Babe, save me—I just called your dad ‘ya 7abibi’ by accident!
vocab.ar: يا بيبي إلحقني—أنا ناديت باباك «يا حبيبي» بالغلط!
vocab.franco: Ya baby el7a2ni—ana nadet babak "ya 7abibi" bel ghalat!

vocab.en: Oh no, I messed up! Sorry about that.
vocab.ar: يا نهار أبيض، غلطت! آسف والله.
vocab.franco: Ya nahar abyad, ghalatt! Asif wallah.

vocab.en: I didn’t mean to say that—my tongue slipped!
vocab.ar: ما قصدتش أقول كده، لساني اتخطى!

vocab.en: Forgive me, I got confused with the names.
I swear I didn’t mean to refuse—your food is amazing!
vocab.ar: والله ما قصدت أرفض، الأكل عندك تحفة!
vocab.franco: Wallah ma 2asadt arfaD, el akel 3andak to7fa!

vocab.en: I’m so embarrassed—let’s just laugh it off!
vocab.ar: أنا خجلان أوي، خلينا نضحك عليها!

vocab.en: Thank you so much for the wonderful day (said to the hosts)
vocab.ar: الف شكر على اليوم الجميل ده
vocab.franco: Alf shokr 3ala el youm el gamil da

vocab.en: God bless your hands (for the food/effort, said to the hostess)
We ate so well, may God keep you (said after a meal)
We had such a great time, we’ll come back soon (promising return)
May God keep your home safe and happy (blessing for the household)
Don’t tire yourself out (said to the hostess as you leave)
We’ll see you soon, God willing (casual but warm)
Take care of yourself (said to elders as you leave)
I’ll call you when I get home (said to partner)
May God keep you all (final blessing before leaving)
Goodbye, stay safe (final farewell)
Darling / Sweetheart (to partner)
Respectful way to address mother-in-law (like 'Mama')
Respectful way to address father-in-law (like 'Baba')
How Egyptians actually say 'I love you' (casual, natural)
Asking 'How is your family?' (as Egyptians say it)
Saying 'God keep them safe' (common after mentioning family)
Eid greeting (to anyone)
Blessing/wish to elders
Complimenting the host's cooking/hospitality
Asking politely for more food
Compliment about how nice everyone looks
Offering to help (useful at family gatherings)

vocab.ar: من غير لحمة، أنا مباكلش لحمة
